title: Introduce temporal profile anchors and changelog atomizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds time-bound profile anchors and an atomizer that emits compact changelog fragments per model variant; improves changelog granularity and reduces noise in release notes.
description:
Context and motivation: Our current model onboarding stores a single canonical performance profile per variant and generates changelogs as large monolithic entries. This makes it hard to track small, time-bound regressions or tune rollouts over narrow windows. ENG-2842 asked for better temporal fidelity in profiles and more concise release notes for rapid rollouts.

What this PR does: Implements 'temporal profile anchors' (lightweight, timestamped profile snapshots tied to a profile lineage) and a 'changelog atomizer' that converts onboarding deltas into small, composable changelog fragments. The atomizer emits fragments grouped by variant and time-window, which the release assembler can later aggregate into human-friendly release notes or machine-readable rollouts.

Design notes: Temporal anchors are stored as compact diffs (profile_v2) and reference the parent profile via a stable anchor_id. Anchors are optimized for storage and fast retrieval by keeping only fields that changed (latency P50/P95, token-cost baseline, infra hints). The atomizer runs as a release-time job (can be invoked from CI or via on-demand CLI), scans anchors within a window, computes deltas against the last published anchor, and produces JSONL fragments with standardized keys (variant, anchor_ts, diff_summary, confidence).

Checklist (what I changed):
- Add temporal anchor model + migration (registry/schema/profile_v2.yaml)
- Anchor creation logic and compact diff serializer (registry/onboard/temporal_anchor.py)
- Changelog atomizer that emits fragments and CLI wrapper (registry/changelog/atomizer.py, scripts/release/emit-changelog-fragments.sh)
- Unit tests for anchor creation/consumption (tests/test_temporal_anchor.py)
- CI check to prevent anchors without required metadata (ci/check-profile-stability.yml)
- Docs describing the small fragment format and recommended aggregation window (docs/onboarding/changelog-format.md)

Commits summary:
- 1a2b3c4: add profile_v2 schema and migration scaffolding
- 4d5e6f7: implement temporal_anchor creation and serializer
- 89ab0cd: implement changelog atomizer + CLI wrapper
- ef01234: add tests and CI gating rule
- 9ab3456: docs and integration notes

Files changed (high-level): registry/onboard/temporal_anchor.py (anchor creation, serialize/deserialize), registry/changelog/atomizer.py (main atomizer logic, windowing, fragment schema), registry/schema/profile_v2.yaml (profile schema extended with anchor metadata), tests/test_temporal_anchor.py (unit coverage > 90% for anchor paths), docs/onboarding/changelog-format.md (consumer-facing doc), scripts/release/emit-changelog-fragments.sh (simple wrapper used by release pipeline), ci/check-profile-stability.yml (lint/gate against missing anchor metadata).

Review highlights and conversation:
- Arjun: Requested that anchors store an explicit upstream-model-hash and a 'rollout_hint' enum so downstream can safely choose fallback variants. I added upstream_hash and rollout_hint to profile_v2 and updated serializer to validate.
- Sofia: Suggested adding a configurable aggregation window (default 24h) and a 'sensitivity' parameter for what constitutes a significant delta; implemented both with sensible defaults and CLI overrides.
- Liam: Asked for size profiling; I ran experiments on 50 models and measured median anchor size of 1.2KB and atomizer throughput of ~1200 anchors/s on a medium CI runner; added results to docs.
- QA: Minor nits on doc wording; addressed and pushed follow-ups.

CI and validation: Pipeline runs include unit tests, flake8, schema lint, and a lightweight integration harness that verifies the atomizer output schema. The CI initially failed due to missing rollout_hint validation; fixed in commit 9ab3456 and re-ran. Final CI status: pass.

Backward compatibility and migration: The migration creates profile_v2 alongside existing profiles and registers anchors only when a profile change is detected. No existing onboarding flows are broken; atomizer is opt-in until release assembler flags are flipped. Migration tooling is included as part of registry/schema/migrate_v2.sh (referenced in docs).

Performance and storage considerations: Anchors are diff-based which reduces storage by ~6x vs naive snapshots in our tests. Atomizer is designed to be parallelizable across variant partitions; we include a simple sharding hint in the fragment output.

Follow-ups and deployment plan:
- Roll out anchor creation to canary onboarding pipelines for two internal models (2 weeks)
- Run atomizer nightly for 30 days and review fragment noise (2 weeks)
- If stable, flip release assembler to consume fragments and enable compact release notes by default (4 weeks)

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Arjun, Sofia, and Liam. All follow-up tasks tracked in ENG-2842 and PM-912.

Notes for reviewers of future changes: Keep the atomizer fragment schema stable (docs/onboarding/changelog-format.md) and prefer new fields via additive changes; when removing fields, add a deprecation window and migration step.
